about: The 12 format prompts from the '12 Claude Video Formats' guide (PDF, signed Simon), shared by the owner on 2026-11-07. The guide ran one prompt 12 times, changing only its last line ('Format: <name>.'): each run was a fresh Claude agent making a 7-second, 540x960 film for an invented coffee roaster as one self-contained HTML file, drawn in code. The 'guide_film' notes describe what those first-try films did, in our words; the guide's images are not copied here. None of these has been made in this repo yet. See studio/formats/README.md and studio/templates/format-prompt.md.
source: 12 Claude Video Formats guide (PDF), shared by the owner on 2026-11-07

formats.name: Kinetic typography
formats.look: The film is built from the words themselves: huge condensed letters fill the frame, stack behind objects and become parts of the set.
formats.guide_film: ROASTED filled the frame; the letters of TUESDAY stacked behind the bag; DOOR ran down the panels of a red door; it ended on a logo card with the bag and a steaming cup.

formats.name: Pixel art game
formats.look: The story becomes a game level: chunky pixels, a HUD with progress and a counter, and dialogue-box text.
formats.guide_film: The delivery was played as a level, from the roaster past a harbour to a front door. A bar along the top ran from TUE to FRI, a bean counter climbed from x00 to x20, and it ended on a title screen.

formats.name: Claymation
formats.look: Everything looks modelled in clay, with swirled fingerprint marks pressed into every surface and objects that come alive.
formats.guide_film: The bag got eyes and travelled by boat from the fire to a door marked FRI. Every surface carried swirled marks, like fingerprints in clay.
formats.notes: Typed as 'Claymation stop motion'. The guide's first try had a moment of plain water at about 2 s.

formats.name: Anime opening
formats.look: An anime title sequence: dramatic skies, speed lines, diagonal split frames, a giant symbol filling the screen and a title card.
formats.guide_film: Green beans turned brown in a fire, a diagonal split crossed the frame, a huge character for fire filled the third beat, and the end had the name in katakana under the logo.

formats.name: Whiteboard sketch
formats.look: A drawn hand and marker build the page stroke by stroke on a whiteboard, with one coloured line tying the story together.
formats.guide_film: The page filled up stroke by stroke, a blue line ran from Tuesday through the days to the cup, and Friday ended up circled in red.

formats.name: 80s VHS commercial
formats.look: An 80s tape ad: the tape machine is part of the story, with PLAY and FF overlays, a tape counter, static and a retro sunset.
formats.guide_film: It opened on a cassette with a 12:00 clock, then PLAY and a tape counter, then static under FF as WED came up: the days passed on fast-forward.
formats.notes: The guide notes static at about 1 s, on purpose.

formats.name: Rubber hose cartoon
formats.look: A 1930s cartoon: everything gets eyes and white gloves, bodies bend like hoses, sunbursts behind, film grain on every frame.
formats.guide_film: The roaster, the bag, the cup and even the boat got eyes, and the cup did a somersault beside the bag. White gloves, big round eyes and film grain over every frame.
formats.notes: The library style rubber-hose already has a demo and an engine (used for Azaadi 1947); use it for a full film.

formats.name: Isometric 3D
formats.look: One connected isometric world seen from a fixed angle, with the subject moving through it like a model railway.
formats.guide_film: The camera angle held as the bag went from conveyor belt to boat to van to a doorway, ending on a small room with the name standing along the tops of its walls.
formats.notes: The slowest of the guide's runs (about 18 minutes).

formats.name: Paper cut-out
formats.look: Layers of cut card with soft shadows under each piece: flames, waves and skies stacked as paper, words on paper strips.
formats.guide_film: Flames, waves and a night sky were stacked as paper layers, THU sat on a paper sun, and the words sat on paper strips.

formats.name: Comic book
formats.look: Comic panels, halftone dots, starbursts, speech bubbles and onomatopoeia that the film invents itself.
formats.guide_film: The journey split into three panels for WED, THU and FRI, with its own sound effects (CRACK!, WHUMP!), which the prompt never asked for.
formats.notes: The guide's appendix prompt shows this format as its example.

formats.name: Neon synthwave
formats.look: A neon road into a striped sunset with a glowing grid on both sides; the road is the timeline.
formats.guide_film: The bag came towards the viewer down the road past signs for WED and FRI, and the scene turned from pink to teal.
formats.notes: Not in the guide's final reel. Its first try had a white flash at about 5 s. The fastest run (about 10 minutes).

formats.name: Liquid motion
formats.look: Liquid is the transition: swirls of it fill the frame and carry the viewer into the next scene.
formats.guide_film: The name sat inside a falling drop, a coffee swirl filled the frame between scenes, and by the end the bag was pouring straight into the cup.
formats.notes: Not in the guide's final reel.
